comments.body: 2026-11-09, read while planning, not built: nothing pushes a linked pane's close across the link. The waiting pane's daemon learns another machine's pane's state only as a Liveness value in a who-style member answer (crates/muster-msg wire.rs:181, across.rs:1866), pulled when somebody asks. Ending the wait needs a design choice: a new message kind that pushes a pane's close to linked daemons, or the waiting daemon polling remote liveness for each declared --until-message-from sender, at a rate and cost to choose.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-10 board review: moved to backlog-lo, still blocked on the push-versus-poll choice in the comment above.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: Since 7def06ab, `report --waiting ... --until-message-from <pane>` ends quietly when that pane closes, but only for a sender on the waiting pane's own daemon. A sender pane on a linked machine (a laptop worker waiting on a devenv reviewer, or the reverse) closing is not seen by the daemon holding the wait, so the wait stands until the 10-minute carry runs out, with the same false 'still waiting' notice to the maker that a_2x1XwUfGo fixed locally. Worth doing if cross-machine reviewers become common.
title: A wait on a message from a pane on a linked machine does not end when that pane closes
